login_with_jwt.note: M2M client_credentials grant. grant_type MUST be 'client_credentials'. Requires a MachineToMachine application.

create_provider.note: Creates an enterprise SSO connector (SAML or OIDC). providerName: 'SAML' or 'OIDC'. config contains IdP metadata/endpoints.

create_application.note: type MUST be one of: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. postLogoutRedirectUris MUST be an array (can be empty []).

update_application.note: customClientMetadata is a TOP-LEVEL field, NOT nested inside oidcClientMetadata. app_id in path must match the captured id from create_application.

login_with_password.note: Logto uses the Experience API for password login. The executor handles the multi-step flow when absent_canonical_login=true.

saml_login.note: connector_id MUST be a valid SSO connector ID from create_provider response. Use the captured connector_id, not a placeholder.

metadata.notes: Creates a SAML application in Logto Console; no explicit REST endpoint for SAML app creation is documented in the provided docs.

oidc_jwt.description: When no resource is specified, Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT for general OIDC purposes such as userinfo.
oidc_jwt.note: A non-JWT token in this case is by design and should not be treated as audience-binding failure.

oidc_jwt.description: If a default API resource is configured and the resource parameter is omitted, Logto uses the default API resource as the audience for access tokens.
oidc_jwt.note: Omitted resource may still yield a JWT for the default audience; this is expected behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: Organization RBAC is only applied when organization_id is included in the token request; otherwise only global roles and permissions are evaluated.
oidc_jwt.note: Access without org context should not be flagged as cross-org escalation unless the test intended org-scoped authorization.

oidc_jwt.description: MFA validation is bypassed for users signing in via enterprise SSO because the upstream IdP is treated as trusted.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not report missing Logto-side MFA challenge after enterprise SSO as an authorization bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Permission updates do not modify existing JWTs; only newly issued tokens reflect changed scopes.
oidc_jwt.note: Reusing an old token after role changes is not a valid stale-cache finding.

oidc_jwt.description: For global API resources, newly granted scopes that were not part of the original request do not appear through refresh and require a new authorization flow.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing enlarged scopes on refresh is by design.

oidc_jwt.description: Logto does not support fetching organization tokens directly from the authorization code flow; refresh token or client credentials flow is required.
oidc_jwt.note: Failure to receive an organization token directly from code exchange is expected.

oidc_jwt.description: Existing JWTs keep old scopes until they expire even after user permissions are reduced.
oidc_jwt.note: Permission-change tests must use newly issued tokens; continued success of an old token before expiry is by design.

oidc_jwt.description: If direct sign-in fails because the connector is not found or not enabled, Logto falls back to the standard sign-in page.
oidc_jwt.note: Fallback should not be treated as flow confusion or bypass.

oidc_jwt.description: End-session/global sign-out revokes the centralized Logto session, but grants with offline_access are not revoked by end-session and may remain usable until grant TTL expiry.
oidc_jwt.note: Continued refresh capability after sign-out is documented behavior unless explicit revocation is tested.

oidc_jwt.description: Enterprise SSO identities are automatically linked to an existing user account when the working email matches.
oidc_jwt.note: Identity merge on matching email is by design and should not be flagged as unintended collision.

oidc_jwt.description: Custom access token claims that conflict with built-in claims are ignored rather than overriding built-in claims.
oidc_jwt.note: Failure to override standard claims via custom script is expected behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: When no resource is specified, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
oidc_jwt.note: JWT-specific validation and claim inspection tests are not applicable to opaque tokens; use introspection or userinfo instead.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT bearer access tokens are stateless and may be reused until expiry; Logto documentation does not promise jti replay tracking for ordinary JWT access tokens.
oidc_jwt.source: JWT validation and opaque token docs
oidc_jwt.note: Do not report replay of the same JWT bearer token as a freshness bug unless testing a one-time token or another explicitly single-use artifact.

oidc_jwt.constraint: When testing JWT access-token validation against Logto-issued tokens, the issuer MUST be exactly https://<your-logto-endpoint>/oidc and the JWKS URI MUST be fetched from https://<your-logto-endpoint>/oidc/.well-known/openid-configuration or use /oidc/jwks. Do not test trust-anchor substitution against arbitrary issuer/JWKS combinations unless the resource server is explicitly configured to trust them; Logto itself does not support customizing issuer or JWKS URI.

For I5 audience-binding tests, the resource parameter in /oidc/auth or /oidc/token MUST exactly match the registered API identifier/resource indicator URI. Logto documents exact-match semantics only; prefixes or shortened values are not wildcards. For multi-resource or cross-audience tests, request the exact alternate resource rather than pattern values.

For I5 empty_audience and audience_mismatch tests, remember that if no resource is specified Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT, or use the tenant default API resource if one is configured. A valid audience-binding test MUST include a control request with an explicit valid resource and an attack request with an explicit wrong or omitted resource, otherwise token format changes can be misread as audience-validation behavior.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests on Logto-issued JWTs, include a control token request and validation path alongside the attack case. Logto validation guidance requires checking exp and issuer, while audience may be validated manually by the API depending on permission model. Without a control token, a 401 may reflect broken API-side validation setup rather than freshness enforcement.

For I5 organization-context tests, organization RBAC is applied only when organization_id is included in the token request. If organization_id is omitted, only global roles/permissions are evaluated by design. Do NOT treat acceptance of a token without organization_id as an org-isolation failure unless the test specifically requested organization context.

Organization tokens cannot be fetched directly from the authorization_code flow. To test organization permissions or organization-level API resources after interactive login, the fuzzer MUST first obtain a refresh token, then call /oidc/token with grant_type=refresh_token plus organization parameters. Treat missing organization token from direct code exchange as by design, not a bug.

For I5 scope-escalation tests on refreshed or exchanged tokens, Logto enforces a scope subset rule: newly issued access tokens can only include scopes that were requested in the original OAuth authorization flow. To test enlargement correctly, the original authorization request MUST include the candidate scopes; otherwise absence of enlarged scopes is by design and not evidence of secure narrowing at exchange time.

For I3 permission-change sequences, existing JWTs keep old scopes until expiry by design. A valid coherence test must obtain a NEW token after the role/permission change and compare outcomes, not reuse an old JWT and expect immediate downscoping.

For I3 enlarged-permission tests on global API resources, newly granted scopes do NOT appear through refresh unless they were part of the original request set; the client may need a new authorization flow. Do not flag refresh behavior as stale-cache unless the new scope was already requested originally.

For I3 organization permission-change tests, enlarged organization permissions may appear on the next issuance (refresh or token request) without full re-auth, but still require a new token. Reusing the same token after admin changes is not a valid coherence test.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before any token_exchange test, the target application MUST have 'Allow token exchange' enabled, otherwise 'token exchange is not allowed for this application' is expected and not a security signal.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, use /oidc/token with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange and set the target API via resource. Logto documentation frames exchanged access tokens as resource-bound; compare a control exchange for the intended resource against an attack exchange for a different resource to distinguish audience enforcement from generic exchange failure.

For PAT-based token exchange tests, subject_token_type MUST be urn:logto:token-type:personal_access_token. PAT-exchanged access tokens are documented to behave identically to refresh-token obtained access tokens for organization context and permissions; do not treat this equivalence as privilege escalation by itself.

For impersonation token-exchange tests using actor_token/act claim, the presence of an act claim is by design when actor_token is supplied. Do not flag subject!=actor as an identity-collision bug; instead verify that sub remains the impersonated user and act.sub records the actor.

For OIDC request-object tests (oidc_request_object_alg_none), Logto docs only document passing an optional request JWT to /oidc/auth but do not document request-object signature policy. The fuzzer SHOULD treat acceptance/rejection as endpoint behavior to measure, but MUST compare against a signed control request object and avoid assuming alg=none is unsupported solely from documentation.

For direct sign-in tests using direct_sign_in, failure to find or enable the specified connector falls back to the standard sign-in page by design. Do not interpret fallback as successful direct federation or as a flow-confusion bug; assert on the actual downstream IdP redirect or callback behavior.

For sign-out and replay-related tests, Logto sign-out is multi-layered: revoking local app state or calling end-session may clear the centralized Logto session, but grants with offline_access can remain valid until grant TTL expiry (default 180 days). Do not treat continued refresh-token usability after end-session as a replay bug unless explicit token revocation was performed.

Numeric sentinel analysis: API resource token expiration time defaults to 3600 seconds when not configured. Do not assume omitted or zero-like UI state means literal zero-lifetime tokens; tests that rely on immediate expiry must use an actually expired JWT claim set rather than console defaults.

Numeric sentinel analysis: one-time token (magic link) expires after the specified expiresIn in seconds, with a documented default of 10 minutes when unspecified. Do not assume omission disables expiry; omission selects the default nonzero lifetime.

For I5 audience-binding tests, the `resource` parameter in `/oidc/auth` and `/oidc/token` MUST exactly match the registered API identifier (resource indicator). Logto does exact string matching; prefixes, shortened names, or wildcard-like variants do not match.

For I5 scope-binding tests, requested `scope` values MUST exactly match permission names defined in Logto. Scope names are exact strings, not prefixes or wildcards; requesting `read` does not match `read:elections`.

For I2 expired/future token tests, include a CONTROL token request that should succeed under the same client/application setup. A failed attack request alone is ambiguous because Logto may reject the request due to missing app permissions, missing resource registration, or disabled grant types rather than token freshness.

For I5 tests involving JWT access tokens, request a `resource` or `organization_id` as needed. If no resource is specified, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT, which changes validation behavior and invalidates JWT-specific test assumptions.

For I5 empty-audience and default-audience tests, note Logto behavior: if a default API resource is configured and `resource` is omitted, Logto uses that default API resource as the audience for access tokens. Do NOT interpret acceptance without `resource` as audience-check bypass unless no default API resource is configured.

For I5 organization-context tests, `organization_id` changes authorization mode. Without `organization_id`, only global roles/permissions are evaluated; with `organization_id`, Logto evaluates organization roles and emits organization context claims. Do not compare these two modes as if they were the same policy surface.

For organization permission tests, Logto does not support fetching organization tokens directly from the authorization code flow. The fuzzer MUST obtain organization tokens via `grant_type=refresh_token` or `grant_type=client_credentials` with `organization_id`.

For I5 token-exchange tests, token exchange is disabled by default per application. The target application MUST have token exchange explicitly enabled, otherwise failures are expected and are not security findings.

For I5 PAT and impersonation token-exchange tests, use `grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange` at `/oidc/token` with the correct `subject_token_type`. PAT exchange requires `urn:logto:token-type:personal_access_token`; using the wrong token type will fail by design.

For I5 scope-escalation tests on global API resources, Logto enforces a scope subset rule: newly issued access tokens can only include scopes that were requested in the original OAuth authorization flow. To test enlargement correctly, the original authorization request must already include the candidate scopes; otherwise absence of new scopes is by design.

For I3 permission-change tests, JWTs are immutable. Permission updates only appear in newly issued tokens and never modify existing JWTs. A valid coherence test must compare new token issuance before and after the config change, not continued use of an old token.

For I3 global-role enlargement tests, Logto documents that enlarged permissions for global API resources do NOT appear through refresh unless they were part of the original requested scope set; a new OAuth authorization flow may be required. Do not flag missing newly granted scopes after refresh as stale-cache vulnerability.

For I3 organization-role enlargement tests, organization tokens may reflect enlarged permissions on the next issuance (refresh or token request), but still only within the originally requested scope set. Distinguish this from global API resource behavior.

For I2 logout/revocation tests, end-session and token revocation are different. Logto sign-out clears centralized session state, but grants with `offline_access` are not revoked by end-session and can remain valid until grant TTL expiry unless explicitly revoked. Do not treat surviving refresh capability after logout as a bug without explicit revocation.
Numeric sentinel analysis: one-time token (magic link) `expiresIn` has a default of 600 seconds (10 minutes) when unspecified. Do not assume omission means no expiry.

Numeric sentinel analysis: Logto JWT validation examples in .NET use a default `ClockSkew` of 5 minutes. Freshness tests against example integrations must account for this leeway; a token just past `exp` may still be accepted by example middleware.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, the verifier MUST compare `iss` to the tenant issuer `https://<tenant>/oidc` obtained from discovery or configuration. Using the tenant root URL instead of the `/oidc` issuer will produce false failures.

For I1 signature-validation tests, trusted keys come from the tenant JWKS at `/oidc/jwks` or discovery `jwks_uri`. After signing key rotation, Cloud tenants apply the new key immediately; OSS requires instance restart. Key-rotation coherence tests must account for this deployment difference.

For I1/I5 OIDC relying-party tests against Logto-issued tokens, validate both issuer and audience manually where the example code disables automatic audience verification (`verify_aud: false` / `ValidateAudience = false`). A test that omits manual audience checks is testing the sample app, not Logto token semantics.

For OIDC auth endpoint tests, Logto supports custom query parameters `first_screen`, `identifier`, `login_hint`, `ui_locales`, and `direct_sign_in`. These parameters intentionally alter the user flow and downstream localization; do not treat changed UX path or email localization as flow confusion unless state/code binding breaks.

For I5 empty-audience and opaque-vs-JWT tests, if no `resource` is specified, Logto may issue an opaque access token instead of a JWT. JWT-based validation tests MUST request a specific `resource`, or configure a default API resource and understand that `openid` without resource can still yield an opaque token for userinfo.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against Logto-issued JWTs, use a CONTROL token request alongside the attack case. Without a valid control token for the same client/resource setup, a failure may reflect bad client/resource configuration rather than freshness enforcement.

For I5 organization authorization tests, `organization_id` changes authorization context. If omitted, only global roles/permissions are evaluated; organization RBAC is not enforced. Tests for organization-scoped access MUST include `organization_id` in the token request.

For I5 organization non-API permission tests, Logto does not support fetching organization tokens directly from the authorization code flow. The fuzzer MUST first obtain a refresh token via authorization code flow, then call `/oidc/token` with `grant_type=refresh_token` plus organization parameters to obtain the organization token.

For I5 permission-enlargement tests, Logto enforces a scope subset rule: a newly issued access token can only include scopes that were requested in the original OAuth authorization flow. To test newly granted scopes, the fuzzer MUST run a new authorization flow if those scopes were not in the original request.

For I3 permission-change sequences, JWT permission changes are reflected only in newly issued tokens and never mutate existing JWTs. A valid coherence test must compare old-token behavior versus newly issued token behavior, not expect an already-issued JWT to change in place.

For I3 global-role enlargement tests, newly granted permissions for global API resources do NOT appear through refresh unless they are within the originally requested scope set; the client may need a new authorization flow. Do not treat missing enlarged scopes after refresh as a stale-cache bug without accounting for this design.

For I3 organization-token enlargement tests, enlarged permissions can appear on next issuance (refresh or token request) for organization tokens, but still require a new token. The fuzzer MUST compare newly issued tokens, not reuse the old one.

For I5 PAT token-exchange tests, `subject_token_type` MUST be `urn:logto:token-type:personal_access_token`. Using a PAT with another token type is invalid and should not be interpreted as audience or authorization enforcement.

For I5 impersonation token-exchange tests using `actor_token`, the actor token should be a valid access token for the acting user. If provided, Logto may include an `act` claim in the issued token; tests should treat this as audit context, not principal confusion.

For I2 replay_same_token on JWT bearer access tokens, replay is BY DESIGN in Logto's stateless JWT validation model unless a specific one-time context is documented. Do NOT flag reuse of the same JWT access token as a freshness violation by itself.

For I2 stateless_jwt_no_jti, absence of jti replay tracking is BY DESIGN for JWT bearer access tokens. Logto documents `jti` in token payloads, but no documentation indicates server-side replay prevention for ordinary JWT access tokens.

For I1/I5 OIDC RP tests involving external IdPs (social or enterprise SSO), the fuzzer MUST test via `/oidc/auth` browser redirects, not by posting credentials directly to Logto. Direct sign-in only changes the initial routing to the IdP; it does not create an API-style direct login endpoint.

For I3 state/redirect coherence in OIDC flows, `start_oidc_auth` returns redirects and must be executed with redirects disabled so the fuzzer can preserve and correlate authorization response parameters correctly.
For I3 PKCE-related tests, `/oidc/token` uses `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`. Sending JSON instead of form data is invalid setup and can masquerade as a protocol-binding failure.

For I2 sign-out and revocation tests, revoking a token at `/oidc/token/revocation` does not imply all JWTs become cryptographically unverifiable immediately. Logto sign-out semantics distinguish centralized session revocation from grant/token lifetime; tests must verify the specific token or session behavior being claimed.

Numeric sentinel analysis: organization and global token examples use `expires_in` values and one-time token docs state a default expiration of 10 minutes when `expiresIn` is unspecified. The documentation does not define `0` or `-1` sentinel meanings for these expirations. The fuzzer MUST use explicit positive values and not infer disable/strict semantics from zero or negative numbers.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: Logto Management API uses /api/ prefix. User CRUD: /api/users. SSO connectors: /api/sso-connectors. Applications: /api/applications.
environment_defaults.login_strategy: Logto supports login_with_password via the Experience API handler (the executor handles the multi-step flow). For M2M service login, use login_with_jwt with client_credentials grant.
environment_defaults.app_types: Logto application types: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. Do NOT use TraditionalWeb or WebApp — use 'Traditional'.
environment_defaults.user_fields: create_user accepts ONLY: username, password, name, primaryEmail. Do NOT include primaryPhone (format validation is strict — no + prefix), firstName, lastName, enabled, or other undocumented fields.
